note: Step 7 speculative fixture (derivation A). No erratum touches p.34. Every assert is derived by hand from the 60-wire topology and the printed rule, not printed against dial pads. Topology: pushbutton 6 (6Y/6+) is the only + feed for RUN (6X/D17, D18/M-) and for the coils (4S/6X, 3S/4S): switch 4 LEFT (4R/2F, 1F/2F) pulls in relays 1 and 2, switch 3 LEFT (3F/3R, 3F..6F) pulls in relays 3-6, each coil returning through its indicator lamp to the 1C-6C/6C/6- minus chain. The selection tree is rooted on minus at 6S (6S/6-): switch 6 picks 6R-5S or 6T-5V, switch 5 picks relay 1 or relay 2 arms, relays 1-2 (switch 4) pick relays 3-6 arms, relays 3-6 (switch 3) pick the pad, so pad = 8*sw3 + 4*sw4 + 2*sw5 + sw6 with LEFT (dash) = 1, which matches every letter on the printed plate. D16/D19 puts the selected pad on the STOP short; on any other contact or gap the motor is driven, so with pushbutton 6 held the wiper can rest only on the selected pad. Output lights: 2V(+) through switch 2 set 2 and switch 1 sets 1/2 to 1A/2A/3A/4A, per the printed character-count table; 5A, 6A unwired. Letters E, N, R (the E-, N- and O-class cases printedUnprinted names) and Q, C, H are a script choice covering all four switch 5/6 branches, both states of every relay level and the all-relays-out pad D0; consecutive pads differ, and each relays-out pad (2*sw5 + sw6, selected until the relays pull in) is at least three pads from the start pad, H aside (its pad is that pad). Switches beyond a letter's length keep their earlier setting. Post-release asserts are the Step 7 note: with no drive and the wiper at rest, the dial does not move (O-R13). Rotary run rate, geometry and coast stay profile fallbacks O-R1, O-R3 and O-R5.
